title: Shortest Distances Between Every Pair
real_world_story: A delivery platform manages restaurants, distribution hubs and customer locations across a region. Riders ask for the fastest travel time between many different pairs of locations, and answers need to be ready instantly. The platform precomputes the shortest travel time between every pair of nodes so any future query can be answered immediately.

real_world_connection.input_represents: A weighted graph of locations with roads and travel times
real_world_connection.query_represents: A frequent request about the fastest travel time between two locations
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Precomputing all-pairs shortest distances in advance

problem_statement: Given a weighted, undirected graph with N nodes, an adjacency matrix where a positive value represents the travel time between two directly connected nodes and 0 represents no direct road, compute the shortest travel time between every pair of nodes. Then answer Q queries, each asking for the shortest travel time between two nodes.
task: Precompute all-pairs shortest distances and answer each query with the minimum travel time.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N. The next N lines each contain N integers forming the adjacency matrix (0 on the diagonal, positive integer travel time between directly connected nodes, 0 for no direct road). The next line contains an integer Q. The next Q lines each contain two integers U and V indicating a query.
output_format: For each query, print the minimum travel time between node U and node V. If they are not connected, print -1.

examples.explanation: The shortest time from node 1 to node 4 is via node 2: 1 + 2 = 3. From node 2 to node 3 it is 1 + 2 + 1 = 3 via node 4, and the shortest time from a node to itself is 0.

expected_algorithm.name: Floyd-Warshall
expected_algorithm.reason: Floyd-Warshall computes the shortest distance between every pair of nodes in O(N^3), allowing many queries to be answered in constant time afterward.

hint: Start with a distance matrix initialized to the direct edge weights.
For each intermediate node K, check whether traveling through K shortens any pair distance.
Update the matrix until every pair holds its shortest distance.
real_world_takeaway: Precomputing all-pairs distances lets a delivery platform answer large numbers of route-time queries instantly instead of recomputing each one separately.
